steps.text: Is that all there is?

steps.name: Calm Nobleman
steps.text: I'm not hiding even a shred of truth from you.
The way this was handled... was quite the surprise.

steps.name: Calm Nobleman
steps.text: How should we proceed now?
How should we proceed? We don't.
This never had anything to do with you to begin with. All we're doing now is making adjustments to how the territory in question will be handled. How does that have anything to do with you?

steps.name: Calm Nobleman
steps.text: You're right about that, but with how things turned out, those Infected will get to stay on that city plate. It'll be difficult to keep them from gossiping about this.
And? Who would believe Infected nonsense?

steps.name: Calm Nobleman
steps.text: Then what shall we do next...?
What shall we do next?
There's no rush. We still have lots to do.

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: That's all I have to report for this incident.

steps.name: Woman
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Woman
steps.text: Have you located the piece that this Czerny man wrote during the incident?

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: The Empresses' Voice is ready to transcribe it at any moment and can personally play it for you in a few hours.

steps.name: Woman
steps.text: No need. I can listen to the recording.

steps.name: Woman
steps.text: Not bad. I can even hear him crying from the bottom of his heart as he wrote the piece.

steps.name: Woman
steps.text: He's a talented man. Too bad he's not quite talented enough.

steps.name: Nervous Infected
steps.text: So how did it go?

steps.name: Dispirited Infected
steps.text: Not bad. It didn't get worse.

steps.name: Dispirited Infected
steps.text: Andante said the infection deterioration caused by the incident was unusual. Most infections went into a continuous, stable phase, and I'm no exception.

steps.name: Nervous Infected
steps.text: It's not going to get worse again like before, right?

steps.name: Dispirited Infected
steps.text: Andante said they looked into the phenomenon pretty thoroughly. Apparently nearly all of the Originium that got activated during the incident has gone into an extended low-activity state.

steps.name: Dispirited Infected
steps.text: In other words, I get to hang around a little longer.

steps.name: Nervous Infected
steps.text: Thank goodness...

steps.name: Nervous Infected
steps.text: Right, does Andante know what the Herzog is going to do with the Afterglow?

steps.name: Dispirited Infected
steps.text: Well, this is just what she said she heard, but apparently the Empresses' Voice has requested the Herzog not lay a finger on the Afterglow.

steps.name: Nervous Infected
steps.text: Oh, thank heavens, and thank Their Majesties' kindness—

steps.name: Dispirited Infected
steps.text: Keep it down!

steps.name: Nervous Infected
steps.text: *Sigh*, what should we do from here on out...?

steps.name: Dispirited Infected
steps.text: Oh, shut up. You don't think things have gotten out of hand enough as is?

steps.name: Dispirited Infected
steps.text: What to do from here on out? Live one day at a time, that's what.

steps.name: Nervous Infected
steps.text: I want to live more than a day, though.

steps.name: Dispirited Infected
steps.text: Then you should really keep your mouth shut.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Hibiscus, I finally get it now. There are some things that you're better off not knowing anything about.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: I guess I'll apply to be transferred somewhere else as soon as I'm done with the follow-up work here.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Maybe I'll go to the landship. That sounds nice.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Don't move.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: It took a lot of effort just to find you.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Do you have anything to say?

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: It was your men who tricked Kreide into coming to Vyseheim, right?

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Everything you said was the truth, except for the bit about payment. You knew he was in a hurry to make money for my treatment, and you lured him into this mess with that.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: But you two had nothing against each other! Why did you do it?!

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: If I told you, I'd have to kill you.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: I don't have much longer to live to begin with.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Alright then. Seeing as we're old colleagues, I will tell you.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Gräfin Strollo was already looking for Kreide, and she was very close to finding him.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: So what? Kreide was always there by my side, and that practically meant you had full control of him!

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: You read her research notes. You know full well just how terrifying her work on the Voice of Mundane was.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Until I got my hands on her notes, all I knew was that she had put a lot of time into researching this subject, but I never knew the true extent of her research.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: If we'd let her continue working, she might just have been able to do something even more appalling with the Voice of Mundane. Say, triggering and inducing Resonanz at much greater ranges.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: You could've woken up in the morning and found your grandson transformed into a monster. Would you have wanted that?

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Rather than letting things come to that, it was much better to bring Kreide right to her. Put the rush on her, and let her put her plan in motion before she could work out the kinks.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: So? Any more questions?

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: What would you have done if Ebenholz hadn't found the amplifiers in the Afterglow Hall?

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: What do you think?

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: However the Afterglow turned out, that's how I would've turned out myself.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: No further questions.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Come with me, then.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Not going to kill me?

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: I've got no reason to kill you, and it would've given me yet another thing to weigh on my conscience.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Come. Let's head to my shop for a cup of coffee. We'll talk about those stupid, honorable young men.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Must I?

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: What do you think?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Lava?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Why'd you push yourself like that? If anything happened to you, I'd never, ever forgive you!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Oh, you're talking about what happened in Vyseheim, right? Look, I'm all fine—

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: And who was it who had a standoff with an angry mob, who didn't evacuate even knowing that she'd be affected by the Voice of Mundane, and who fought those people even though she barely learned any Arts?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I don't remember telling you any of this...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: I already talked to Mr. Czerny! He told me everything!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Uh... If you wanted to know all the whys and wherefores, why didn't you come talk to me directly?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: I actually visited Mr. Czerny to ask him about my piano teacher in Leithanien, Mr. Johann, and it was only after we kept talking that I found out you almost—

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Almost...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: —I'm warning you! If something like this happens again, don't you dare push yourself like that! Y-You hear me?! You hear me?!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Alright, don't cry anymore. Look, see? I'm alright.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: But your infection—!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Yes, it's got rather severe thanks to the Voice of Mundane, but it's under control now, so...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: No! That's not enough! You're always on my case about my health, but you don't care about what happens to you at all!

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: If you... If I lost you... I... I...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Lava, I promise you I'll look out for myself more, okay?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Really.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Don't you dare lie to me!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Why would I? The Doctor gave me quite a long holiday, you know? I'm going to spend this time well and get some quality rest in.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Alright, now, you said you asked him about Mr. Johann? How is he?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Mr. Czerny said he saw Mr. Johann at a gathering a year ago and that he was fine and well.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Speaking of, you went all the way to Leithanien yourself and even got a flute for your wand. Did you learn how to play while you were there?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You mean this?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: The most I'm doing with it is treating it as a wand. I don't know how to play.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Of course really.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: You're just being shy, aren't you?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Why would I be shy about this?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: I don't believe you! Play something!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Well... Alright, here goes...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Alright!

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: That's the worst sound I've ever heard in my life!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Thanks for your concern, Doctor. I'm feeling very well.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: And I must thank you again for the protection you are offering the Afterglow.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: If you and Rhodes Island hadn't intervened, the Empresses' Voice would never have lifted a finger for my home.

options: Just doing my job.
Helping the Infected is Rhodes Island's creed.
The Afterglow is a lot easier to handle than Ebenholz.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: You're too humble.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: It's exactly as you said, and I'm starting to appreciate that more and more.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I suppose there must be a reason you summoned me here?

options: You asked to be deployed to the front lines, and I have to confirm your intentions.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I've already written my thoughts in full on the report.

options: Your condition's stable, but your infection's serious.
Anything can happen in battle.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I'm prepared.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Truth be told, Doctor. When Hibiscus helped me up and walked me to the concert hall, I was already prepared to die.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Even though so much has happened, and things turned out nothing like I had imagined, I... lived.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: It really feels quite peculiar, and I cannot describe it very well, whether through words or music.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I'm not expecting to find how to express this feeling on the battlefield, but I'm thinking that it might prove beneficial if I try to fight for the Infected in an entirely different way.

options: I understand how you feel.
But do wait for your evaluation results.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Speaking of which, Ebenholz is here too, is he?

options: Of course.
Why do you ask?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I haven't seen him at all since the day after we arrived at Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Sometimes, I can't help but think that the black-clad Graf Urtica might have actually died.

options: According to Leithanien's official reports, he's indeed gone.
He's alive and well. Give him some time.
Ironically, that actually helped get our cooperation with Leithanien on track.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: You're right.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Well then, I'll take my leave now, Doctor.

options: Speaking of Ebenholz, it happens the next thing on my agenda has to do with him.
Do you want to see him?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Never mind. I don't dare to claim I know how much this incident has affected him. I can only imagine.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: If there comes a day when he's willing to see me or Hibiscus, we'll talk then.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Goodbye, Doctor.

options: Goodbye.
I look forward to hearing the music you'll write off the battlefield, and hope it'll be no less impressive than your past work.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Doctor? I'm surprised you found me here.

options: Some nice, fresh air with all the wind here. Helps destress.
There's an Operator who saw you here.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I don't need destressing.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Have you got nothing to say to me?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Who? I don't mind having a little chat.

options: I digress. I'm a Messenger today. Here's a letter for you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: A letter? Where is it from?

options: Leithanien.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I have an idea what it is. Hand it over.

options: Need me to stay and open it with you? One of my many services.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You're a funny one.

options: I get that a lot.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I really can't imagine you in a fight... Are you always this lighthearted when you're out commanding battles?

options: Haha.
I wouldn't mind you getting a little less serious when you're off to a field operation.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Is this how you always react when you're embarrassed?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You have that hood on, and you hardly ever say a word. Hmm hmm. It's quite imposing.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Well, I look forward to it, then.

options: I'm going then. Enjoy your alone time.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: That goes without saying.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: This... is the passport of a Leithanian citizen... Ebenholz.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Kreide's... and Graf Urtica's... death certiﬁcates.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hm? There's more?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: A letter?

a.text: Congratulations on the freedom that you have been longing for.
I am writing this letter to inform you that our common enemy, Graf Urtica, has passed away.
I would like to extent my sincerest apologies to you in regard to the troubles he and his friends have brought about.
It is my hope that this letter and the file enclosed may reach you as a consolation.
P.S. Please ensure that the death of Graf Urtica remains a cold hard fact.
Otherwise our joint effort will eventually go down the drain.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It's not signed... An anonymous letter?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Just my impression of her.
Rhodes Island Operator Ebenholz presses the tip of his wand to the letter and sets it ablaze.
Not long after, the flames reach the passport, then the Count of Urtica's death certificate, and then Kreide's.
The smell of burning paper spreads across the deck.
Ebenholz picks up the cello next to him.
He thinks back to how his dear friend played the cello, closes his eyes, and begins to play a simple, lively melody.
When the Twin Empresses first took control, countless pieces of music singing their praises sprung up all over Leithanien. This, too, is one of those pieces.

Today, the second half of the song has long been forgotten. Only the first half is still sung by a small number of people, thanks to its uplifting melody and the lyrics openly express the singer's cheerful mood.
The sunset is glaringly bright.
